/** A color by its index in the palette file (0–63). */
export function endesga(index: number): string {
  const color = ENDESGA_64[index]
  if (color === undefined) throw new Error(`Endesga 64 has no color ${index}`)
  return color
}

# Art provenance: `examples/base-2d`

| Asset | Where | Made by | How | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wick (idle ×2, two run frames, jump, fall) | `sprites.ts` | Claude (AI coding agent), integration thread, PR #10 (M1.8) | Drawn as a palette-indexed pixel map in source, previewed as PNGs, no generation API and no reference image | 2026-10-11 |
| Stone (three variants), moss cap, edges, grass, glowing mushroom, vine | `sprites.ts`; placed by `src/render/tiles.ts` | Same | Same; placement is a deterministic autotiler (`tiles.test.ts`) | 2026-10-11 |
| Ember crystal | `sprites.ts` | Same | Same | 2026-10-11 |
| Night backdrop (dithered sky bands, stars, moon, ruined towers, trees, fog), light shafts, fireflies, particles | `src/render/backdrop.ts`, `renderer.ts`, `particles.ts` | Same | Drawn in code from palette colors at fixed positions | 2026-10-11 |
| Pixel lights and vignette | `src/render/light-levels.ts`, `pixels.ts` | Same | Computed: a stepped falloff with a 4 × 4 Bayer dither (`light-levels.test.ts`), tinted with palette colors | 2026-10-11 |
| Palette | `palette.ts` | Endesga ([Lospec](https://lospec.com/palette-list/endesga-64)), supplied by the Owner | Copied from `docs/art/palettes/endesga-64.txt`; `art.test.ts` checks it | 2026-10-11 |
| Pixelify Sans (screens' type) | `@fontsource/pixelify-sans` 5.3.0 | Stefie Justprince, via Fontsource | OFL-1.1, bundled by Vite | 2026-10-11 |

Why pixel maps rather than a generation API: the base's sprites are tiny (8 × 8 and 16 × 16) and must use Endesga 64 exactly. Image generators produce off-palette, anti-aliased output that would need quantizing and cleanup by hand, so the art was authored directly on the palette instead. The Owner may still replace any of it; generated art goes through the `pipelines` gates once they exist (M3), with its provenance recorded here.

Look (second pass, 2026-10-11): the first pass read as a Bubble Bobble and Celeste clone (a bubble-blowing blob with a red scarf, pink bricks, a bubble goal), and the Owner asked for something less derivative and more like a current itch.io hit. Now: Wick, a hooded wanderer with glowing eyes and a lantern, climbs mossy ruins at night to an ember. Modern pixel-art treatment: colored outlines and rim light, a multiplied light map with dithered pixel lights (lantern, ember, mushrooms, fireflies, moon), light shafts, parallax layers, a vignette, afterimages, landing shake and sparks. Bubble Bobble (one single-screen room) and Celeste (movement feel, squash and stretch, dust) remain as influences, not as copied motifs. Owner acceptance of the look is open.

// The base's art, as palette-indexed pixel maps: each character in a row is a key into the sprite's palette
// (Endesga 64 colors only, checked by art.test.ts), and `.` is transparent. Pixel maps in source keep the art
// diffable and exactly on palette; the renderer turns them into textures. Provenance: PROVENANCE.md.
//
// The look (2026-10-11, after the Owner asked for something less like a clone): Wick, a small hooded wanderer
// with glowing eyes and a lantern, climbs mossy ruins at night to an ember. The renderer adds the light.

export interface PixelSprite {
  readonly width: number
  readonly height: number
  /** Key → `#rrggbb`, every value an Endesga 64 color. */
  readonly palette: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
  readonly rows: readonly string[]
}

function sprite(palette: Readonly<Record<string, string>>, rows: readonly string[]): PixelSprite {
  return { width: rows[0]?.length ?? 0, height: rows.length, palette, rows }
}

// A scripted run from the start to the goal (the ember), as (direction, jump held, ticks) segments. It pins the
// sim's behavior: the golden tests replay it and compare the final state hash, in Node and in Chromium, WebKit
// and Firefox (determinism is cross-engine, AGENTS.md). The browser journeys replay it with real key presses.
// Any change to movement, the room or the plugin changes the hash on purpose: investigate it, never rebaseline
// it per engine.
import type { MoveInput } from './sim/index.ts'

export type RouteSegment = readonly [x: MoveInput['x'], jump: boolean, ticks: number]

export const GOLDEN_ROUTE: readonly RouteSegment[] = [
  [1, false, 30], // walk right, out from under the first platform
  [-1, true, 14], // jump back left onto it
  [-1, false, 20],
  [1, false, 12],
  [1, true, 16], // up and right to the second
  [1, false, 12],
  [0, false, 10],
  [1, false, 25],
  [1, true, 16], // the third
  [1, false, 12],
  [0, false, 10],
  [1, false, 30],
  [1, true, 16], // the fourth, by the right wall
  [1, false, 8],
  [0, false, 10],
  [-1, false, 4],
  [-1, true, 18], // back left to the fifth
  [-1, false, 10],
  [0, false, 10],
  [-1, false, 24],
  [-1, true, 18], // the top platform
  [-1, false, 30], // and into the ember
]

/** The route as one input per tick. */
export function routeInputs(route: readonly RouteSegment[] = GOLDEN_ROUTE): MoveInput[] {
  return route.flatMap(([x, jump, ticks]) => Array.from({ length: ticks }, () => ({ x, jump })))
}

/** The tick the golden route touches the goal on. */
export const GOLDEN_GOAL_TICK = 342

 */

| Asset | Where | Made by | How | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crate (8 × 8, moss band, one brace) | `sprites.ts` | Claude (AI coding agent), M2.1b physics demo thread | Drawn as a palette-indexed pixel map in source, in base-2d's Emberwick style; no generation API and no reference image | 2026-10-11 |
| Stone of lantern glass (8 × 8) | `sprites.ts` | Same | Same | 2026-10-11 |

Endesga 64 only, checked by `art.test.ts` against `docs/art/palettes/endesga-64.txt`. Everything else on screen (the room, Wick, the light) is base-2d's, recorded in `examples/base-2d/src/art/PROVENANCE.md`. Pixel maps rather than a generation API for the same reason base-2d gives: at 8 × 8 a generator's off-palette, anti-aliased output would need redrawing by hand anyway. The Owner may replace either sprite.

import { Flow, type ScreenDef } from '@mcthaydt/automata-runtime'
import { Effect } from 'effect'

export const pausedScreen: ScreenDef = {
  id: 'paused',
  pausesSim: true,
  enter: (ctx) =>
    Effect.gen(function* () {
      const flow = yield* Flow

      const div = document.createElement('div')
      div.className = 'af-screen-frame'
      div.setAttribute('data-screen-frame', '')
      div.setAttribute('data-testid', 'paused-screen')

      const header = document.createElement('div')
      header.className = 'af-screen-frame__header'
      const h1 = document.createElement('h1')
      h1.textContent = 'Paused'
      header.appendChild(h1)

      const body = document.createElement('div')
      body.className = 'af-screen-frame__body'
      const p = document.createElement('p')
      p.textContent = 'Simulation is paused.'
      body.appendChild(p)

      const actions = document.createElement('div')
      actions.className = 'af-action-bar'
      actions.setAttribute('data-testid', 'actions')
      const resumeBtn = document.createElement('button')
      resumeBtn.className = 'af-control af-control--primary'
      resumeBtn.setAttribute('data-kind', 'primary')
      resumeBtn.setAttribute('data-testid', 'resume-btn')
      resumeBtn.setAttribute('data-action', 'resume')
      resumeBtn.textContent = 'Resume'
      resumeBtn.onclick = () => flow.dispatch('resume')
      actions.appendChild(resumeBtn)

      div.appendChild(header)
      div.appendChild(body)
      div.appendChild(actions)
      ctx.layer.appendChild(div)

      yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => Effect.sync(() => div.remove()))
    }),
}

import { Flow, type ScreenDef } from '@mcthaydt/automata-runtime'
import { Effect } from 'effect'
import { resetActiveSim } from './play.ts'

export const titleScreen: ScreenDef = {
  id: 'title',
  enter: (ctx) =>
    Effect.gen(function* () {
      resetActiveSim()
      const flow = yield* Flow
      const div = document.createElement('div')
      div.className = 'af-screen-frame'
      div.setAttribute('data-screen-frame', '')
      div.setAttribute('data-testid', 'title-screen')

      const header = document.createElement('div')
      header.className = 'af-screen-frame__header'
      const h1 = document.createElement('h1')
      h1.textContent = 'Boot & Flow Demo'
      header.appendChild(h1)

      const body = document.createElement('div')
      body.className = 'af-screen-frame__body'
      const p = document.createElement('p')
      p.textContent = 'A blank game demonstrating the runtime boot sequence and flow transitions.'
      body.appendChild(p)

      const actions = document.createElement('div')
      actions.className = 'af-action-bar'
      actions.setAttribute('data-testid', 'actions')
      const playBtn = document.createElement('button')
      playBtn.className = 'af-control af-control--primary'
      playBtn.setAttribute('data-kind', 'primary')
      playBtn.setAttribute('data-testid', 'play-btn')
      playBtn.setAttribute('data-action', 'play')
      playBtn.textContent = 'Play'
      playBtn.onclick = () => flow.dispatch('play')
      actions.appendChild(playBtn)

      div.appendChild(header)
      div.appendChild(body)
      div.appendChild(actions)
      ctx.layer.appendChild(div)

      yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => Effect.sync(() => div.remove()))
    }),
}
